summary: Sh. Ali Mashhour continues his discussion on the book of Salah, focusing on the definition and significance of the Adhan (the Islamic call to prayer). He explains that linguistically, Adhan means to announce something, and in Islamic jurisprudence, it is specifically the announcement made with particular words to indicate the time of prayer. Sh. Ali Mashhour discusses the narration of Malik, a young man who visited the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and received instructions about prayer, including that one person should make the Adhan and the most knowledgeable in Quran should lead the prayer. The speaker emphasizes that the criteria for leading prayer are: the best reciter of Quran, then the most knowledgeable in Sunnah, then the earliest in Hijra, and finally the oldest in age—a principle he notes is often neglected in modern Muslim practice. Sh. Ali Mashhour also explains the historical significance of Adhan as a marker of Islamic identity, noting that the Prophet would observe whether villages made Adhan when deciding military strategy.
suggested_title: The Definition and Significance of Adhan in Islamic Jurisprudence
